diagnosis: The prior cleanup succeeds and the candidate's strict [200,200] plus result-cache-row assertion passes. The new control incorrectly assumed cached_statements=0 disables this old CPython cache. CPython 3.10.22 clamps every capacity below five to five and evicts the least-used entry. Exact default/zero-capacity re-preparation counts are not a portable contract.

upstream_evidence.fact: Capacity values below 5 are replaced with 5.
Entries are reordered by usage count and a least-used entry is evicted when full.

repair: Explicitly use a five-entry capacity-limited control. Require exactly 200 initial preparations and more preparations on the second pass without assuming a version-specific eviction count. Keep the candidate's exact [200,200], strict changing bound-value check on every query, and all transaction, rollback, external-commit, schema, custom-connect, native and pager assertions. Rename the test to state the capacity-limited comparison.
interpretation: This is an invented preparation-reuse mechanism test. The control proves re-preparation under a deliberately undersized cache; it does not claim real workload thrashing, an end-to-end speedup or any performance-gate acceptance. The two preceding failed sources and observations remain preserved.
log_encoding: Exact decoded UTF-8 string returned by the GitHub job-log connector, with no appended newline or rewriting; not a raw HTTP-byte claim.
